classification.difficultyReason: Form the square-minus-inscribed-circle area model; reverse it using ordinary algebra and the positive square root.

spec.description: Planar square with inscribed tangent circle; only the four corner regions are mathematically shaded. Centre point retained.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens only; no derived radius or area given in diagram.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area of the shaded region, correct to 2 decimal places, if the square has side length 10 cm.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the side length of the square, correct to 2 decimal places, if the area of the shaded region is 100 cm².

answer.worked:
Let the positive square side be $s$ cm; the inscribed circle radius is $\frac{s}{2}$ cm.
$$\begin{aligned}100&=s^2-\pi(s/2)^2\\s^2&=\frac{100}{1-\pi/4}\\s&=\sqrt{\frac{100}{1-\pi/4}}\approx21.59\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}$$
